title: Dialog Schema
description: Schema for Dialog domain modeling: attributes, concepts, rules, formulas, and relations.

Attribute.description: A relation elevated with domain-specific invariants. An attribute's identity is structural: (the, type, cardinality).

the.description: The relation in domain/name format (e.g. 'diy.cook/quantity'). Max 64 bytes total. Domain: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, dots; must start with a letter. Name: lowercase kebab-case (no dots); must start with a letter.

cardinality.description: Cardinality of the attribute. Defaults to 'one' when omitted.

as.description: Value type of the attribute. If omitted, any type is allowed.

optional.description: Whether this field is set-widened: a missing claim yields a row with the field bound to absent rather than dropping the row. Required fields (the default) omit this. Marking a field optional changes the concept's identity.

conforms.description: A concept the field's target entity must satisfy — a concept-typed field, written as the target's `concept:{hash}` URI. Entity-valued attributes only, and mutually exclusive with `optional`: the join over "edge exists AND target conforms" is absence over a derived predicate, which stratification has to own first. Enforced structurally, by conjoining the target's premises onto the field.

Cardinality.description: 'one' means asserting a new value retracts the prior claim. 'many' means new claims accumulate alongside existing ones.

Assert.description: The asserted value type for an attribute. Currently only scalar types are supported. Concept references and symbol enumerations are planned future extensions.

ScalarType.description: Built-in scalar types from the dialog domain. 'Text' is shorthand for 'dialog/Text', etc.

ConceptRef.description: Reference to a concept. Can be dot-prefixed (.Ingredient) for current domain, or fully qualified (diy.cook/Ingredient).

SymbolEnum.description: [Future extension, not yet supported] A fixed set of fully qualified symbol values (e.g. ["diy.cook/tsp", "diy.cook/mls"]).

Concept.description: A composition of attributes sharing an entity. An entity matches a concept if and only if it has claims satisfying all required attributes.

with.description: The concept's attributes, required and optional alike. An entity must have claims satisfying every REQUIRED attribute to match; optional ones are marked per-attribute with "optional": true. At least one required attribute must be declared.

NamedRelations.description: Map of field names to attribute descriptors (inline) or attribute references (string paths).

AttributeRef.description: Reference to a pre-defined attribute. '.' means same-named attribute under the current domain. '.name' resolves within current domain. 'domain/name' is fully qualified.

Rule.description: A deductive rule that derives conclusions from existing information through pattern matching, computation, and logical composition.

deduce.description: The conclusion: a concept instance the rule derives when its body is satisfied.

when.description: Conjunction of premises. All must be satisfied by the same variable bindings.

unless.description: Exclusion patterns. If any can be satisfied, the result is filtered out (negation as failure).

reduce.description: Aggregation. Each entry names a head field and the fold defining it. The grouping set is DERIVED — the head fields absent from `reduce` — so a field cannot be both grouped and reduced. Omitted for a plain rule.

FormulaRef.description: Reference to a built-in formula by name.

ConstraintRef.description: Reference to a built-in constraint by name.

Premise.description: A single premise in a rule body. Combines an assertion (what to match) with named term bindings (how to bind variables).

assert.description: What to match: a concept (inline definition), a formula reference, or a constraint reference.

where.description: Named terms mapping field names to variables or constants. For concepts, names correspond to the concept's attribute names. For formulas and constraints, names correspond to their parameter names.

math/sum.description: Adds two integers: is = of + with.

is.description: Derived: sum of the two operands.

math/difference.description: Subtracts second from first (saturating at 0): is = of - subtract.

math/product.description: Multiplies two integers: is = of * times.

math/quotient.description: Divides first by second: is = of / by. Produces no result when divisor is zero.

math/modulo.description: Remainder of division: is = of % by. Produces no result when divisor is zero.

text/concatenate.description: Joins two strings: is = first ++ second.

text/like.description: Glob pattern match. Produces a result only when the pattern matches. '*' matches any sequence, '?' matches a single character.

is.description: Derived: the matched text (empty if no match).

EqualityConstraint.description: Equality constraint, referenced as '==' in a premise's assert field. Asserts two terms must hold equal values. Can filter (both bound), infer (one bound, one free), or fail (neither bound). Used via { "assert": "==", "where": { "this": ..., "is": ... } }.

Term.description: A term is either a variable or a constant value.

Variable.description: A query variable. Variables are bound by the query engine. The same variable appearing in multiple positions requires unification. A blank variable { "?": {} } matches any value without binding.

name.description: Variable name. When omitted, acts as a blank (wildcard) that matches any value without binding.

where.description: Constraints narrowing what this variable admits. Absent means unconstrained.

Constant.description: A concrete value: string, number, or boolean.

Claim.description: A claim in the associative layer. An assertion that has been incorporated by the transactor. Composed of a relation (the), an entity (of), a value (is), and provenance (cause).

of.description: The entity this claim is about.

is.description: The value being linked to the entity through this relation.

cause.description: Provenance describing who produced this claim and when.

Provenance.description: Provenance of a claim, capturing when and where it was produced. Establishes partial order across a distributed system.

by.description: DID of the operator or session authority that produced the claim.

period.description: Coordinated time component: last synchronization cycle.

moment.description: Uncoordinated local time component: moment within a period.

TypeConstraint.description: Constraints on a variable, all conjoined. A record of fixed slots: each appears at most once, and two constraints on one slot merge rather than accumulate. Every slot but `type` narrows the admissible type set as a side effect (a prefix implies a textual type, conformance implies entity, an order bound implies a comparable type); a constraint whose narrowing empties the set is rejected.

domain.description: Constrains the domain half of an attribute (the part before `/`). Symbol-typed values only.

is.description: The domain, written WITHOUT a trailing slash. The separator is an encoding detail supplied on the way in.

name.description: Constrains the name half of an attribute (the part after `/`). Symbol-typed values only.

case.description: Which of the two name forms. A name beginning with an uppercase byte is a fractional position (an ordered relation's member); a lowercase byte is a symbol (a named predicate). The classes are disjoint and exhaustive, so one domain scan serves both and this narrows to a contiguous key range. Absent admits either.

starts-with.description: Lexical prefix every admitted value must begin with. Narrows the type set to those with a lexical form (text, symbol, entity). For attributes prefer `domain`/`name`, which say the same thing structurally.

as.description: Concepts the value's entity must conform to. An ARRAY here is an INTERSECTION: every listed concept must be satisfied. Entity-typed values only. Enforced structurally (the target's premises are conjoined into the query), not as a per-row test.

>=.description: Inclusive lower bound. Comparable types only.

>.description: Strict lower bound. Comparable types only.

<=.description: Inclusive upper bound. Comparable types only.

<.description: Strict upper bound. Comparable types only.

TypeSet.description: The set of types a variable admits. An OBJECT here is a UNION: a value matching any present key is admitted, and intersecting two sets keeps the keys they share. Values are per-variant parameter records, empty today and the place future parameters (an integer width, say) would go. An empty object is the uninhabited set. Omitting `type` leaves the variable untyped.

record.description: Structured data, opaque to the query layer.

symbol.description: A symbol — the type attributes carry, distinguishing them from ordinary strings.

option.description: The absence atom: a row-level absent value. Present alongside other members, it marks the variable optional.

ConformanceRef.description: One conformance obligation, keyed by the target concept's URI (`concept:{hash}`). The value is a parameter record, empty today.

ReduceSpec.description: One fold: the aggregator to apply and the term supplying its input, one lookup per body row.

of.description: The term supplying the fold's input.

Aggregator.description: The fold applied to a group. Absent inputs are skipped. `count` and `sum` have identities, so their head field may be required; `min`, `max`, and `avg` do not, so over an input admitting absence their head field must be optional. `min`/`max` need comparable values, `sum`/`avg` numeric ones.
